newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 20.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
RIFT OVER REFORMS MAY BRING DOWN GOVERNMENT

Differences over econnmic policies may cause the United Front (UF) government's downfall. The Tamil Manila Congress (TMC), a major UF partner, has threatened to pull out of the coalition if Left parties do not stop criticising TMC leader and Union Commerce Minister P Chidambaram on economic reforms undertaken by the UF government. The TMC was particularly sore over the Left for targeting the commerce minister while questiong the policies of the ruling coalition.
The Times Of India
CONGRESS CHIEF REPLACES YOUTH WING LEADER

Congress president Sitaram Kesari replaced B.S. Bitta with Satyajit Gaekwad as Youth Congress president. Gaekwad, a parliament member from Vadodara, Gujarat, is related to the former princely family of Baroda. The removal of Bitta, a staunch loyalist of former prime minister and Congress Parliamentary Party chief Narasimha Rao, is being seen as part of Kesri's bid to assert supremacy over the party.
The Hindustan Times
COURT GRANTS RAO BAIL IN FORGERY CASE

The Delhi High Court granted bail to former Premier Narasimha Rao, former Union minister K K Tewary, guru Chandraswami and his ally K N Aggarwal in the St. Kitts forgery case. Imposing strict conditions for bail, the court asked them to surrender their passports to the Central Bureau of Investigation and not leave the country without the trial court's permission. The court also directed the accused to cooperate in the investigations.
The Economic Times
PRIVATE SECTOR FOR ROAD SECTOR PROJECTS

The government plans to set up companies with private sector participation for executing road sector projects. The exact size of equity participation has not been decided. Also under study is a business plan to leverage two million rupees allocated to the National Highway Authority of India in the 1996 Budget.
IDBI SIGNS $150 MLN SYNDICATED LOAN

The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) signed a $150 million, seven-year syndicated loan facility. The loan, placed primarily in Europe, carried a coupon of 60 basis points over the six-month US$ Libor. IDBI sources said the price was the finest achieved by an Indian borrower for a seven-year maturity. The loan facility would have call and put options at the end of five years, sources added.
FOUR ASIAN BANKS CLEARED TO OPERATE IN INDIA

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved in principle for four Asian banks to set up operations in India. They include two Korean banks - Hanil Bank and Commercial Bank of Korea, Japanese bank - and Sumitomo Bank and Peoples Bank of Sri Lanka. Under the Uruguay Round of Gatt, India had committed to issuing at least eight licences every year. However, licences issued have been way above this limit, sources said. The four foreign banks are the first to be cleared by the RBI this year.
FOREIGN EXCHANGE REGULATIONS ACT TO BE REVISED

Tough provisions of the Foreign Exchange Regulations Act (FERA) will be revised, the revenue secretary assured Indian industry. He said it was not the government's intention to carry out large-scale raids against companies, thereby shaking the confidence of the corporate sector. Too much distinction, he said, should not be made between losses suffered in Indian currency and those in foreign exchange terms. Stating the need for the government to look at the gamut of economic offence related laws, he added it should be examined whether current regulations were suited to the country's needs.
INDIAN OIL CORP'S ECB LIMIT RAISED TO $2.5 BLN

The finance ministry has decided to allow the Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) an enhanced short-term external commercial borrowing limit of $2.5 billion. IOC, the country's sole canalising agency for oil imports, had been asking for a new limit of $3 billion from the current figure of $2 billion. Sources said the enhanced limit had been allowed primarily on account of more expensive petroleum product imports during the current fiscal year, 1996/97 (April-March).
U.S. WEST AGREES ON BPL MOBILE BRAND

BPL-U.S. West Cellular have agreed use the BPL Mobile brand name for its mobile phone service. BPL-U.S. West would pay a licence fee to BPL Cellular Holdings (BPLCH), which in turn would pay 80 percent of that to group flagship BPL. BPLCH's offer document for its American Depository Receipts issue said the licence fee, close to 100 million rupees per annum, would be charged to all its subsidiaries. The bulk of this fee, about 80 million rupees, would come from BPL-U.S. West, which, with the cellular phone licences for Maharashtra, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, constituted the largest business under BPLCH. Payment of this licence fees would start from April 1998, before which the use of the brand name would be free.
DRAFT BROADCAST BILL FOR 25 PCT FOREIGN EQUITY

A 25 percent foreign equity limit has been stipulated in the draft broadcast bill expected to be tabled during the winter session of parliament. This foreign equity can be brought only in media companies incorporated in the country. The draft bill says companies without licences would not be permitted to enter the radio or television segment of the media. These licences would be issued only to companies that fit the corporate structure mentioned in the bill. The draft also proposes the setting up of a broadcasting authority to control all activities of the media industry.
Financial Express
BHARATI TELECOM TO OPPOSE STERLING TAKEOVER BID

Bharati Telecom (BTL) said it would oppose Sterling's open offer for purchase of its shares before the stock market regulator (SEBI). It said Sterling's offer violated the government's telecommunication policy as well as SEBI's takeover guidelines. BTL was also considering a legal recourse to thwart the Sterling bid.
BOWTHORPE GOES ON A BUYING SPREE IN INDIA

British-based Bowthorpe Plc has acquired a majority holding in a New Delhi-based company, Control Group, to launch its controls and switch gears in the Asia-Pacific region. The new company, Wago, formed after a 26-74 tie up between Control Group and Bowthorpe will manufacture and market Bowthorpe's products in the country. Sources said Bowthorpe had plans for acquiring majority stake in at least 12 companies in India, by the year end. Bowthorpe chief executive Nicholas K Brookes said the company would shortly enter the power distribution segment in the country.
INDIAN PORTS NEED $14 BLN INVESTMENT

Indian ports need $14 billion over the next 15 years to set up facilities to handle anticipated cargo traffic of 850 million tonnes by the year 2002. According to government sources, half the projected investment will come from the state agencies and the rest from the private sector. The capacity in the major ports was overstretched leading to heavy congestion, sources added. Given the current six to seven percent annual economic growth rate, the cost of additional capacity to cater to the traffic needs of ports in the next five years would be over 120 billion rupees, they said.
Business Standard
VIDESH SANCHAR NIGAM PLANS GDR LAUNCH IN FEBRUARY

The launch of Videsh Sanchar Nigam's (VSNL) global depository receipt (GDR) issue is planned for February, 1997, because of the delay to STET's international offering. The $5 billion float from STET, earlier planned for January/February 1997, was deferred to end-1997. This would leave a window open at the markets, which VSNL could take advantage of, market sources said. Uncertainty, however, exists on what the size of the VSNL offering would be but estimates are that the primary offering would be lower than what was planned earlier. The GDR issue would be in the range of $200 million, with the government keen to divest another 8250 million.
The Observer
WORLDTEL OFFERS $2 BLN TELECOM PROJECT FOR KERALA, WB, UP

WorldTel has offered to set up a $2 billion basic telecom service project for the states of Kerala, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh (East). WorldTel, a London-based organisation floated by the International Telecom Union, has proposed to enter into a joint venture with public sector company Telecom Consultants India Ltd for the purpose. The basic service joint venture would provide training for Indian telecom personnel.
